web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: What the Price Assumes — Reverse DCF & Peer Multiples
question: What growth rate and margin durability does ANET's $167.66 share price embed after deducting stock-based compensation, RSU dilution, and NVIDIA/Meta competition?

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get.
epigraph.author: Warren Buffett

web_blocks.title: 7.1 Deconstructing $167.66: Reset Multiples After the 18.2% Weekly Drop

web_blocks.html: At the November 20, 2026 close of $167.66 ($167.62 in Finviz), Arista Networks carries a $211.82 billion market cap [22][23]. Subtracting $14.36 billion in cash and marketable securities—with zero debt—leaves an enterprise value of $197.46 billion [2][22]. Trailing twelve-month results show $11.89 billion in revenue, $4.75 billion in net income, and $5.02 billion in gross free cash flow [22]. After an 18.17% weekly selloff from $204.89, shares trade at 45.02x trailing P/E, 37.22x EV/EBITDA, 16.60x EV/Sales, and 42.21x P/FCF [22][23]. Consensus FY2027 EPS of $6.02–$6.05 implies a 27.70x Forward P/E and a 0.77 PEG ratio [22][24].

Even after that reset, Arista trades 10% to 21% above its five-year norms of 40.5x–43.5x trailing P/E and 13.7x EV/Sales [25]. Two opposing forces drive that tension. Positively, Q3 2026 revenue surged 58.5% YoY to $3.66 billion with a 44.9% GAAP operating margin, and RPO reached $8.6 billion [2][3]. Negatively, 9M 2026 GAAP gross margin compressed 160 bps YoY to 62.9%, while CFO conversion fell to 104.8% as customer evaluation inventory doubled to $874.3 million [2]. Meanwhile, NVIDIA's November 17 Form 8-K disclosed Meta expanding Spectrum-X and BlueField-4 alongside NVLink Fusion for custom XPUs [30]. That competitive shift limits multiple re-expansion while buybacks stay paused at $0 against $1.7 billion of unamortized RSUs [2].

web_blocks.title: 7.2 Reverse DCF: Deducting 4.0% SBC, RSU Dilution & Evaluation-Inventory Friction

web_blocks.html: A rigorous Reverse DCF must deduct real economic dilution rather than modeling gross cash flow over basic shares. In 9M 2026, gross free cash flow was $3,792.5 million on $9,402.3 million of revenue (40.3% margin), while stock-based compensation rose 24.0% YoY to $379.4 million (4.0% of revenue) [2]. Corporate buybacks stayed paused at $0 against $1.7 billion of unamortized RSUs (24.3 million unvested shares) [2]. Basic shares therefore expanded by 6.9 million, pushing Q3 diluted shares to 1,278.2 million [2]. Deducting 4.0% SBC from a 41.0% normalized gross FCF margin lowers owner FCF margin to 37.0%. We apply that 37.0% margin across 1.2782 billion diluted shares. At a 9.5% WACC (5.04% 10-year Treasury plus 4.46% ERP) and 3.5% terminal growth, $167.66 still embeds a steep 16.24% 10-year revenue CAGR ($53.5B Year-10 sales) [22][37].

Accounting for SBC and working-capital friction cuts fair value sharply. At 17.2% 10-year CAGR (9.5% WACC), pre-SBC basic DCF is $199.84. However, ex-SBC diluted DCF drops to $179.35 (~$180.00 Base Target, or 29.8x FY27E EPS). That sits just +0.88% above the $177.78 30-week SMA. We also quantify working-capital risk on $874.3 million of evaluation inventory (+116.6%) and $11.4 billion of purchase commitments [2]. A 20%–30% write-down on evaluation gear alone costs $175M–$262M ($0.14–$0.21/share). A 10%–20% write-down across $11.4B commitments costs $1.14B–$2.28B ($0.89–$1.78/share). Worse, a recurring -200 bps FCF margin drag from gross-margin erosion and working-capital tie-ups (35.0% FCF margin) trims Base DCF by -$9.09/share to $170.26. That same 35.0% margin drives a 12.0% CAGR, 10.0%-WACC Bear value of $109.31 (-34.8% vs. CMP).

web_blocks.title: Ex-SBC Diluted Reverse DCF Implied Growth & Stress-Tested Fair Value
web_blocks.the_number: At 37.0% ex-SBC FCF margin and 1.2782B diluted shares (9.5% WACC), $167.66 implies a 16.24% 10-year revenue CAGR. A 17.2% CAGR solves to $179.35 (~$180.00 Base Target).
web_blocks.how_calculated: Discount 10 years of unlevered ex-SBC FCF (Revenue x 37.0% margin) plus Gordon Growth terminal value (Year 10 FCF x 1.035 / (WACC - 0.035)) at 9.5% WACC, add $14.36B net cash, and divide by 1.2782B diluted shares.
web_blocks.the_inputs: TTM revenue $11.89B [22]; gross normalized FCF margin 41.0% less 4.0% 9M 2026 SBC = 37.0% ex-SBC FCF margin [2]; net cash $14.36B [2]; 1.2782B Q3 diluted shares [2]; 10Y Treasury 5.04% [37] + 4.46% ERP = 9.5% WACC.
web_blocks.the_range: Ex-SBC Base (17.2% CAGR, 9.5% WACC) is $179.35 (~$180 Base). Bull (19.6% CAGR) is $212.43 (~$215 Bull). Bear (12.0% CAGR, 10.0% WACC) is $114.91 (~$115 Bear). Under a -200 bps GM/eval-inventory drag (35.0% FCF margin), Base falls to $170.26 and 10.0%-WACC Bear falls to $109.31.
web_blocks.if_off: If Meta Spectrum-X/NVLink Fusion slows 10-year CAGR to 12.0% while gross margin breaks below 61% (35% FCF margin, 10% WACC), fair value drops to $109.31 (-34.8% vs. CMP).

web_blocks.takeaway: Deducting 4.0% SBC and using 1.2782B diluted shares cuts Base DCF from $199.84 to $179.35 (+7.0% vs. CMP; +0.88% above $177.78 30W SMA), leaving no margin of safety at $167.66 or even at Pivot S1 ($153.61) against a >=1.0x ATR stop.

web_blocks.title: 7.3 Peer Comparison: Every Networking & AI Compute Peer Now Sits in Stage 4

web_blocks.html: The November 13–20 selloff erased Arista's lone Stage 2 chart premium. ANET joined Broadcom ($304.41, 15.75x Forward P/E [38]), Cisco ($90.64, 14.88x Forward P/E [39]), HPE ($40.91, 8.60x Forward P/E [40]), Celestica ($201.63, 9.09x Forward P/E [41]), Jabil ($225.76, 10.24x Forward P/E [42]), and NVIDIA ($125.53, 7.56x Forward P/E [43]) in Stage 4 [22][23]. Without a Stage 2 scarcity edge, ANET's 27.70x Forward P/E and 16.60x EV/Sales look rich. Its forward multiple sits nearly double Broadcom (15.75x Forward P/E, 48.57% operating margin) and more than triple NVIDIA (7.56x, 66.15% operating margin) [22][38][43]. Even after cutting our Base Target from $242 to $180 (~29.8x FY27E EPS), Arista still embeds a substantial multiple premium over every peer in its cohort.

web_blocks.caption: Peer Valuation, Profitability & Stage Comparison (As of 2026-11-20) [22][38][39][40][41][42][43]
web_blocks.takeaway: ANET carries the richest Forward P/E (27.70x) and P/E TTM (45.02x) across the cohort while all seven peers sit in Stage 4, capping multiple expansion near our $180.00 ex-SBC Base fair value.

web_blocks.mechanism: During the 1998–2000 telecom and internet buildout, Cisco's revenue compounded >45% annually and its P/E expanded past 100x; when carrier capex froze in 2001, revenue dropped 30% sequentially and valuation compressed to ~20x.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Cisco peaked near $80/share (~$555B market cap, >100x P/E) in March 2000 before falling ~88% to $8.60 in October 2002 despite remaining profitable.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Even elite networking franchises suffer sharp multiple compression when capex visibility wobbles; ANET at 27.7x forward P/E is far saner than 100x in 2000, but $11.4B in purchase commitments and $874.3M evaluation inventory mean any hyperscaler pause could compress P/E toward 19x (~$115).

book_paragraphs: When a high-flying market leader falls 18.2% in a single week, your first instinct might be to call it a bargain. Before making that leap, you have to ask two disciplined questions: what did the old price overlook, and what does $167.66 still assume once we deduct real dilution? At the November 20, 2026 close, Arista Networks carries a $211.82 billion market value, or $197.46 billion after subtracting its $14.36 billion debt-free cash pile.

On trailing twelve-month results of $11.89 billion in sales, $4.75 billion in net income, and $5.02 billion in gross free cash flow, the stock trades at 45.02 times trailing earnings and 27.70 times consensus FY2027 earnings of roughly $6.05 per share. That multiple looks cheaper than a week ago, yet once we account for stock-based compensation, zero buybacks, gross-margin compression, and NVIDIA's November 17 competitive disclosures, $167.66 offers no margin of safety.

That five-to-six percentage-point gap between gross cash generation and true owner earnings explains why headline P/E ratios often mislead investors during late-cycle network upgrades. Arista still delivers extraordinary capital efficiency and zero debt, yet shareholders only capture cash flow net of employee equity dilution and working-capital pre-builds. When evaluation hardware sits on hyperscaler floors for two or three quarters before final acceptance, cash conversion temporarily outpaces or lags reported gross margin, masking the competitive pricing pressure captured in our stress cases. Therefore, anchoring valuation on a 37.0% ex-SBC owner free cash flow margin and 1.2782 billion diluted shares removes accounting optimism without penalizing Arista’s genuine engineering leadership. Every input across the 28-cell discounted cash flow sensitivity matrix confirms the same discipline: paying $167.66 per share demands nearly 16.2% compounded annual growth for a full decade, leaving zero margin of safety if white-box switching or co-packaged optics slows wallet-share expansion after 2027.

book_subsections.title: Deducting Stock-Based Compensation and Real Share Dilution
paragraphs: In our earlier model, we credited Arista with a 41.0% gross free cash flow margin over 1.2634 billion basic shares, which produced a $199.84 Base DCF. That shortcut ignores a crucial shift in Arista's 2026 cash flow statement: management paused share buybacks completely at zero dollars in the first nine months of 2026 while nine-month stock-based compensation climbed 24% to $379.4 million, or 4.0% of revenue, leaving $1.7 billion of unamortized RSUs across 24.3 million unvested shares.

With zero buybacks to offset equity awards, basic shares grew by 6.9 million and Q3 diluted share count reached 1.2782 billion. Deducting that 4.0% SBC cost cuts true owner free cash flow margin from 41.0% to 37.0%, and dividing by 1.2782 billion diluted shares at a 9.5% discount rate cuts our 17.2%-growth Base DCF from $199.84 down to $179.35. Even at $167.66 today, the stock still embeds a 16.24% ten-year compound revenue growth rate—leaving barely 7% upside to Base fair value and less than 1% upside above the $177.78 30-week moving average.

book_subsections.title: Why We Cut Our Base Target to $180 and Model a $109 Stress Floor
paragraphs: Unbiased re-underwriting requires lowering fair value when competition intensifies and costs rise. NVIDIA's November 17 Form 8-K revealed that Meta—16% of Arista's FY2025 sales—plans expanded Spectrum-X and BlueField-4 networking, while NVLink Fusion extends NVIDIA's rack fabric to custom XPUs. At the same time, Arista's nine-month GAAP gross margin fell 160 basis points to 62.9%, customer evaluation inventory doubled to $874.3 million, and purchase commitments hit $11.4 billion.

Anchoring our 12-month Base Case at $180.00 matches our $179.35 ex-SBC diluted DCF and values Arista at nearly 30 times FY2027 consensus earnings. In a bullish distributed-inferencing scenario where growth reaches 19.6% annually, ex-SBC fair value reaches $215.00. In a bearish capex-digestion cycle (12.0% growth at a 10.0% discount rate), fair value drops to $115.00—and adding a 200-basis-point gross-margin and evaluation-inventory drag (35.0% FCF margin) lowers stressed intrinsic value to $109.31, roughly 35% below today's price.

book_subsections.title: Losing the Stage 2 Scarcity Premium Against Broadcom and NVIDIA
paragraphs: Compare Arista side by side with its networking and silicon peers after the November 20 selloff. Every single company in the seven-stock peer table—Broadcom, Cisco, HPE, Celestica, Jabil, NVIDIA, and Arista—now sits in Stage 4. Without a Stage 2 uptrend to justify scarcity pricing, Arista's 27.70 times forward P/E stands nearly double Broadcom's 15.75 times (at a higher 48.57% operating margin) and more than triple NVIDIA's 7.56 times (at a 66.15% operating margin).

Arista's 28.89% ROIC and $14.36 billion net cash cushion still warrant a premium over legacy hardware vendors like Cisco and HPE, yet trading at roughly 30 times FY2027 earnings in our $180 Base Case leaves little room for multiple expansion until gross margins stabilize and evaluation gear converts to revenue.

callouts.title: The Cisco 2000 Base Rate: Why Multiples Compress Faster Than Profits
callouts.text: During the 1998–2000 network buildout, Cisco grew sales past 45% a year and peaked above 100 times earnings. When carrier budgets froze in 2001, Cisco stayed profitable, yet the stock dropped 88% because its valuation compressed to 20 times. Arista at 27.7 times forward earnings is nowhere near a 2000-style bubble, yet $11.4 billion in non-cancellable supplier commitments ensures that any hyperscaler digestion in 2027 would compress the multiple toward 19x (~$115).
